es.summary: Trastorno genético autosómico recesivo que reduce la producción de alfa‑1 antitripsina, predisponiendo a enfermedad pulmonar obstructiva crónica y daño hepático.
key_points: Disminución de AAT permite daño alveolar por elastasa neutrófila
Acumulación de AAT mal plegada en hepatocitos causa cirrosis
Mayor riesgo de COPD, especialmente en lóbulos inferiores
El tabaquismo acelera la progresión pulmonar
Se trata con reposo de AAT, evitar humo y manejo de cirrosis

pathophysiology: Mutación del gen SERPINA1 → proteína AAT mal plegada
Disminución de inhibición de elastasa → destrucción de paredes alveolares
Acumulación de AAT en hepatocitos → inflamación y fibrosis hepática
risk_factors: Tabaquismo activo o exposición a humo de segunda mano
Exposición crónica a polvo o contaminantes
signs_symptoms: Disnea de esfuerzo y tos crónica
Sibilancias y sensación de opresión torácica
Hepatomegalia, ictericia y elevación de enzimas hepáticas
diagnostics: Radiografía de tórax: enfisema en lóbulos inferiores
Pruebas hepáticas: AST/ALT, fosfatasa alcalina elevadas
treatment: Evitar todo tipo de humo y contaminantes
Terapia de reemplazo de AAT por infusión intravenosa
Broncodilatadores y corticoides inhalados para COPD
Manejo de cirrosis: restricción de sal, diuréticos, posible trasplante
complications: Cirrosis hepática y riesgo de carcinoma hepatocelular
Desnutrición por aumento del gasto energético
nursing_care: Evaluar patrón respiratorio, SpO2 y auscultación cada turno
Monitorizar gases arteriales y signos de hipoxemia
Educar sobre abstinencia de tabaco y evitar irritantes
Vigilar signos de insuficiencia hepática (ictericia, edema)
Posicionar en semi‑Fowler para facilitar expansión pulmonar
patient_teaching: No fumar y evitar ambientes con humo o polvo
Importancia de la vacunación anual contra gripe y neumococo
Reconocer empeoramiento de disnea o tos y buscar ayuda médica
Adherir al programa de reemplazo de AAT según indicación
Dieta baja en sal y evitar alcohol para proteger el hígado

outcomes: NOC: Patrón respiratorio eficaz – mantener SpO2 ≥ 92 % en reposo
NOC: Capacidad de tolerar actividad – caminar 100 m sin disnea excesiva

interventions.action: Monitorizar SpO2 y frecuencia respiratoria cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta hipoxemia temprana y permite intervención rápida

interventions.action: Administrar terapia de reemplazo de AAT según prescripción
interventions.rationale: Aumenta la inhibición de elastasa y protege el tejido pulmonar

interventions.action: Enseñar respiración diafragmática y ejercicios de expansión torácica
interventions.rationale: Mejora la ventilación y reduce el trabajo respiratorio

interventions.action: Promover abstinencia de tabaco y evitar exposición a contaminantes
interventions.rationale: Previene la progresión del daño pulmonar

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente en semi‑Fowler (30‑45°)
interventions.rationale: Facilita la expansión pulmonar y mejora la oxigenación

interventions.action: Registrar y reportar cualquier aumento de disnea o cambios en esputo
interventions.rationale: Permite detección precoz de exacerbaciones

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: NOC: Balance hídrico – peso estable ± 0.5 kg/semana
NOC: Integridad de la piel – sin edema periférico ni úlceras

interventions.action: Evaluar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada turno
interventions.rationale: Detecta desequilibrio hídrico temprano

interventions.action: Monitorizar peso diario y presencia de edema
interventions.rationale: Identifica retención de líquidos y ascitis

interventions.action: Restringir sodio a <2 g/día y registrar consumo
interventions.rationale: Previene acumulación de líquido y ascitis

interventions.action: Administrar diuréticos según orden médica y observar respuesta
interventions.rationale: Promueve eliminación de exceso de líquido

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de descompensación hepática (aumento de abdomen, ictericia)
interventions.rationale: Facilita búsqueda de atención oportuna

interventions.action: Mantener la piel limpia y seca; cambiar posición cada 2 h si hay edema
interventions.rationale: Previene lesiones cutáneas y úlceras por presión

en.summary: Autosomal recessive genetic disorder that reduces production of alpha‑1 antitrypsin, predisposing to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and liver damage.
key_points: Reduced AAT allows neutrophil elastase‑mediated alveolar damage
Misfolded AAT accumulates in hepatocytes causing cirrhosis
Higher risk of COPD, especially in lower lobes
Treatment involves AAT replacement, avoidance of smoke, and cirrhosis management

pathophysiology: SERPINA1 gene mutation → misfolded AAT protein
Reduced elastase inhibition → destruction of alveolar walls
Accumulation of AAT in hepatocytes → inflammation and hepatic fibrosis
risk_factors: Active smoking or second‑hand smoke exposure
Chronic exposure to dust or pollutants
signs_symptoms: Wheezing and sensation of chest tightness
Hepatomegaly, jaundice, and elevated liver enzymes
Basal emphysema visible on chest X‑ray
diagnostics: Liver function tests: AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase elevated
treatment: Avoid all forms of smoke and pollutants
AAT replacement therapy via intravenous infusion
Bronchodilators and inhaled corticosteroids for COPD
Cirrhosis management: salt restriction, diuretics, possible transplant
complications: Hepatic cirrhosis and risk of hepatocellular carcinoma
Malnutrition due to increased energy expenditure
nursing_care: Assess respiratory pattern, SpO2, and auscultation each shift
Monitor arterial blood gases and signs of hypoxemia
Educate on smoking cessation and avoidance of irritants
Monitor signs of hepatic failure (jaundice, edema)
Position in semi‑Fowler to facilitate lung expansion
patient_teaching: Do not smoke and avoid smoke or dusty environments
Importance of annual flu and pneumococcal vaccination
Recognize worsening dyspnea or cough and seek medical help
Adhere to AAT replacement program as prescribed
Low‑salt diet and avoid alcohol to protect the liver

outcomes: NOC: Effective breathing pattern – maintain SpO2 ≥ 92 % at rest
NOC: Ability to tolerate activity – walk 100 m without excessive dyspnea

interventions.action: Monitor SpO2 and respiratory rate every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detect early hypoxemia and allow rapid intervention

interventions.action: Administer AAT replacement therapy as prescribed
interventions.rationale: Increase elastase inhibition and protect lung tissue

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and chest expansion exercises
interventions.rationale: Improve ventilation and reduce work of breathing

interventions.action: Promote smoking cessation and avoidance of pollutants
interventions.rationale: Prevent progression of lung damage

interventions.action: Position patient in semi‑Fowler (30‑45°)
interventions.rationale: Facilitate lung expansion and improve oxygenation

interventions.action: Document and report any increase in dyspnea or sputum changes
interventions.rationale: Allow early detection of exacerbations

outcomes: NOC: Fluid balance – weight stable ± 0.5 kg/week
NOC: Skin integrity – no peripheral edema or ulcers

interventions.action: Assess intake and output each shift
interventions.rationale: Detect early fluid imbalance

interventions.action: Monitor daily weight and presence of edema
interventions.rationale: Identify fluid retention and ascites

interventions.action: Restrict sodium to <2 g/day and record intake
interventions.rationale: Prevent fluid accumulation and ascites

interventions.action: Administer diuretics per order and observe response
interventions.rationale: Promote elimination of excess fluid

interventions.action: Educate patient on signs of hepatic decompensation (abdominal swelling, jaundice)
interventions.rationale: Facilitate timely medical attention

interventions.action: Keep skin clean and dry; change position every 2 h if edema present
interventions.rationale: Prevent skin lesions and pressure ulcers

key_points.1.quote: AAT deficiency may also cause a liver disease called cirrhosis .

key_points.2.quote: Unlike smoking-related COPD, COPD caused by alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency typically only affects the lower lobes of the lungs (Agarwal et al., 2023).

key_points.3.quote: If your liver doesn't make enough AAT, your lungs may be more easily damaged from smoking , pollution , or dust from the environment.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AAT deficiency, or AATD) is an inherited condition that raises your risk for lung and liver disease.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Most cases are linked to cigarette smoking , though COPD can occur in people who have never smoked.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: If your liver doesn't make enough AAT, your lungs may be more easily damaged from smoking , pollution , or dust from the environment.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: These symptoms may include: Wheezing Shortness of breath , especially after exercise Chronic cough with phlegm (mucus) Repeated respiratory infections such as colds and the flu Chest pain Fatigue Faster-than-normal heartbeat when you stand up Vision problems Losing weight without trying Some people who have AAT deficiency may have liver damage.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: These symptoms may include: Wheezing Shortness of breath , especially after exercise Chronic cough with phlegm (mucus) Repeated respiratory infections such as colds and the flu Chest pain Fatigue Faster-than-normal heartbeat when you stand up Vision problems Losing weight without trying Some people who have AAT deficiency may have liver damage.

sections.diagnostics.1.quote: AAT deficiency is caused by changes in the SERPINA1 gene , which carries instructions for making the AAT protein.

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: If the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity (FEV 1 /FVC) is under 0.7, or 70 percent of predicted, COPD is present.

sections.treatment.0.quote: To help prevent or delay lung damage, it is important to quit smoking (if you smoke) and avoid secondhand smoke , dust, and air pollution.

sections.treatment.2.quote: Inhaled corticosteroids are commonly used to decrease airway swelling and are used as long-term therapy.

sections.complications.0.quote: When alveolar walls become damaged and lose elasticity, resulting in problems with exhalation and CO 2 trapping, emphysema occurs ( Figure 11.19 ).

sections.complications.4.quote: Because of the increased effort required to breathe, patients with chronic COPD can develop muscle wasting and cachexia , a disorder that causes loss of muscle and adipose tissue ( Figure 11.20 ).

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: When a low oxygen level is present or suspected, pulse oximetry and arterial blood gas analysis can provide helpful information that can guide therapy, including oxygen administration.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: Educational topics include smoking cessation, infection prevention, vaccination, and how to use inhaled medications.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: To help prevent or delay lung damage, it is important to quit smoking (if you smoke) and avoid secondhand smoke , dust, and air pollution.
